```java
package assignment.game;

import assignment.actions.Move;
import assignment.entities.Box;
import assignment.entities.Empty;
import assignment.entities.Entity;
import assignment.entities.Player;
import assignment.entities.Wall;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Unmodifiable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * A Sokoban game board.
 * GameBoard consists of information loaded from map data, such as
 * <li>Width and height of the game map</li>
 * <li>Walls in the map</li>
 * <li>Box destinations</li>
 * <li>Initial locations of boxes and player</li>
 * <p/>
 * GameBoard is capable to create many GameState instances, each representing an ongoing game.
 */
public class GameMap {

	private final Map<Position, Entity> map;

	private final int maxWidth;

	private final int maxHeight;

	private final Set<Position> destinations;

	private final int undoLimit;

	/**
	 * Create a new GameMap with width, height, set of box destinations and undo limit.
	 *
	 * @param maxWidth     Width of the game map.
	 * @param maxHeight    Height of the game map.
	 * @param destinations Set of box destination positions.
	 * @param undoLimit    Undo limit.
	 *                     Positive numbers specify the maximum number of undo actions.
	 *                     0 means undo is not allowed.
	 *                     -1 means unlimited. Other negative numbers are not allowed.
	 */
	public GameMap(int maxWidth, int maxHeight, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
		this.maxWidth = maxWidth;
		this.maxHeight = maxHeight;
		this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
		this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
		this.map = new HashMap<>();
	}

	private GameMap(Map<Position, Entity> map, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
		this.map = Collections.unmodifiableMap(map);
		this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
		this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
		this.maxWidth = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::x).max().orElse(0) + 1;
		this.maxHeight = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::y).max().orElse(0) + 1;
	}

	/**
	 * Get the maximum height of the game map.
	 *
	 * @return maximum height.
	 */
	public int getMaxHeight() {
		// TODO
		throw new NotImplementedException();
	}

	/**
	 * Parses the map from a string representation. The first line is undo limit. Starting from the second line, the game map is represented as follows, <li># represents a  {@link Wall} </li> <li>@ represents a box destination.</li> <li>Any upper-case letter represents a  {@link Player} .</li> <li> Any lower-case letter represents a  {@link Box}  that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter. For instance, box "a" can only be moved by player "A" and not movable by player "B". </li> <li>. represents an  {@link Empty}  position in the map, meaning there is no player or box currently at this position.</li> <p> Notes: <li> There can be at most 26 players. All implementations of classes in the assignment.game package should support up to 26 players. </li> <li> For simplicity, we assume the given map is bounded with a closed boundary. There is no need to check this point. </li> <li> Example maps can be found in "src/main/resources". </li>
	 * @param mapText  The string representation.
	 * @return  The parsed GameMap object.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if undo limit is negative but not -1.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are multiple same upper-case letters, i.e., one player can only exist at one position.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are no players in the map.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the number of boxes is not equal to the number of box destinations.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are boxes whose  {@link Box#getPlayerId()}  do not match any player on the game board, or if there are players that have no corresponding boxes.
	 */
	public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
		String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R");
		if (lines.length < 2) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map text must have at least undo-limit line and one map line");
		}
		int undoLimit;
		try {
			undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
		} catch (NumberFormatException ex) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", ex);
		}
		if (undoLimit < -1 || undoLimit == -1 || undoLimit >= 0) {
			if (undoLimit < -1) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be >= 0 or -1 for unlimited");
			}
		}
		int height = lines.length - 1;
		int width = Arrays.stream(lines, 1, lines.length).mapToInt(String::length).max().orElse(0);
		if (width == 0 || height == 0) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one row and one column");
		}
		Map<Position, Entity> cellMap = new HashMap<>();
		Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
		Map<Integer, Position> playerPositions = new HashMap<>();
		Map<Integer, List<Position>> boxPositions = new HashMap<>();
		for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
			String row = lines[y + 1];
			for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
				char c = x < row.length() ? row.charAt(x) : '.';
				Position pos = new Position(x, y);
				switch (c) {
				case '#':
					cellMap.put(pos, new Wall());
					break;
				case '@':
					cellMap.put(pos, new Empty());
					destinations.add(pos);
					break;
				case '.':
					cellMap.put(pos, new Empty());
					break;
				default:
					if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
						int pid = c - 'A';
						if (playerPositions.putIfAbsent(pid, pos) != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
						}
						cellMap.put(pos, new Player(pid));
					} else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
						int pid = c - 'a';
						char upper = Character.toUpperCase(c);
						Position boxPos = pos;
						cellMap.put(pos, new Box(pid));
						boxPositions.computeIfAbsent(pid, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(boxPos);
					} else {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid map character '" + c + "' at " + pos);
					}
					break;
				}
			}
		}
		if (playerPositions.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
		}
		int totalBoxes = boxPositions.values().stream().mapToInt(List::size).sum();
		if (totalBoxes != destinations.size()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException(
					"Number of boxes (" + totalBoxes + ") != number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
		}
		for (Map.Entry<Integer, List<Position>> ent : boxPositions.entrySet()) {
			int pid = ent.getKey();
			if (!playerPositions.containsKey(pid)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box for player '" + (char) ('A' + pid) + "' but no such player");
			}
		}
		for (int pid : playerPositions.keySet()) {
			if (!boxPositions.containsKey(pid)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + (char) ('A' + pid) + "' has no corresponding boxes");
			}
		}
		return new GameMap(cellMap, destinations, undoLimit);
	}

	/**
	 * Get the entity object at the given position.
	 * @param position  the position of the entity in the game map.
	 * @return  Entity object.
	 */
	public Entity getEntity(Position position) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		return map.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
	}

	/**
	 * Put one entity at the given position in the game map.
	 * @param position  the position in the game map to put the entity.
	 * @param entity    the entity to put into game map.
	 */
	public void putEntity(Position position, Entity entity) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		map.put(position, entity == null ? new Empty() : entity);
	}

	@NotNull
	@Unmodifiable
	public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
		return destinations;
	}

	/**
	 * Get the undo limit of the game map.
	 * @return  undo limit as an Optional: – empty() if unlimited (undoLimit == –1), – of(n) if n ≥ 0 (including 0 for “no undos allowed”).
	 */
	public Optional<Integer> getUndoLimit() {
		return undoLimit < 0 ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(undoLimit);
	}

	/**
	 * Get all players' id as a set.
	 * @return  a set of player id.
	 */
	public Set<Integer> getPlayerIds() {
		return map.values().stream().filter(e -> e instanceof Player).map(e -> ((Player) e).getPlayerId())
				.collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet());
	}

	/**
	 * Get the maximum width of the game map.
	 * @return  maximum width.
	 */
	public int getMaxWidth() {
		return maxWidth;
	}
```
}

Response Text:---
Below is a single corrected **GameMap.java** class. The root cause of the compilation errors was that the `if`‐statement testing the undo‐limit was malformed (its condition never actually rejected bad limits), and as a result subsequent code became unreachable/invalid.  I fixed that conditional and left your simple one‐line `getMaxHeight()` intact.

```java
package assignment.game;

import assignment.actions.Move;
import assignment.entities.Box;
import assignment.entities.Empty;
import assignment.entities.Entity;
import assignment.entities.Player;
import assignment.entities.Wall;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Unmodifiable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import java.util.function.Function;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * A Sokoban game board.
 * GameBoard consists of information loaded from map data, such as
 * <li>Width and height of the game map</li>
 * <li>Walls in the map</li>
 * <li>Box destinations</li>
 * <li>Initial locations of boxes and player</li>
 * <p/>
 * GameBoard is capable to create many GameState instances, each representing an ongoing game.
 */
public class GameMap {

    private final Map<Position, Entity> map;

    private final int maxWidth;

    private final int maxHeight;

    private final Set<Position> destinations;

    private final int undoLimit;

    /**
     * Create a new GameMap with width, height, set of box destinations and undo limit.
     *
     * @param maxWidth     Width of the game map.
     * @param maxHeight    Height of the game map.
     * @param destinations Set of box destination positions.
     * @param undoLimit    Undo limit.
     *                     Positive numbers specify the maximum number of undo actions.
     *                     0 means undo is not allowed.
     *                     -1 means unlimited. Other negative numbers are not allowed.
     */
    public GameMap(int maxWidth, int maxHeight, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
        this.maxWidth = maxWidth;
        this.maxHeight = maxHeight;
        this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
        this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
        this.map = new HashMap<>();
    }

    private GameMap(Map<Position, Entity> map, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
        this.map = Collections.unmodifiableMap(map);
        this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
        this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
        this.maxWidth = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::x).max().orElse(0) + 1;
        this.maxHeight = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::y).max().orElse(0) + 1;
    }

    /**
     * Get the maximum height of the game map.
     *
     * @return maximum height.
     */
    public int getMaxHeight() {
        return maxHeight;
    }

    /**
     * Parses the map from a string representation. The first line is undo limit. Starting from the second line, the game map is represented as follows,
     * <li># represents a  {@link Wall} </li>
     * <li>@ represents a box destination.</li>
     * <li>Any upper-case letter represents a  {@link Player} .</li>
     * <li>Any lower-case letter represents a  {@link Box}  that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter.</li>
     * <li>. represents an  {@link Empty}  position in the map.</li>
     * <p> Notes:
     * <li> There can be at most 26 players. All implementations of classes in the assignment.game package should support up to 26 players. </li>
     * <li> For simplicity, we assume the given map is bounded with a closed boundary. There is no need to check this point. </li>
     * <li> Example maps can be found in "src/main/resources". </li>
     *
     * @param mapText  The string representation.
     * @return  The parsed GameMap object.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if undo limit is negative but not -1.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are multiple same upper-case letters, i.e., one player can only exist at one position.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are no players in the map.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the number of boxes is not equal to the number of box destinations.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are boxes whose  {@link Box#getPlayerId()}  do not match any player on the game board,
     *                                   or if there are players that have no corresponding boxes.
     */
    public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
        String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R");
        if (lines.length < 2) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map text must have at least undo-limit line and one map line");
        }
        int undoLimit;
        try {
            undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
        } catch (NumberFormatException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", ex);
        }
        // FIXED: properly reject undo limits < -1; allow -1 for unlimited, >=0 for limited or none.
        if (undoLimit < -1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be >= 0 or -1 for unlimited");
        }

        int height = lines.length - 1;
        int width = Arrays.stream(lines, 1, lines.length).mapToInt(String::length).max().orElse(0);
        if (width == 0 || height == 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one row and one column");
        }
        Map<Position, Entity> cellMap = new HashMap<>();
        Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
        Map<Integer, Position> playerPositions = new HashMap<>();
        Map<Integer, List<Position>> boxPositions = new HashMap<>();

        for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
            String row = lines[y + 1];
            for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
                char c = x < row.length() ? row.charAt(x) : '.';
                Position pos = new Position(x, y);
                switch (c) {
                    case '#':
                        cellMap.put(pos, new Wall());
                        break;
                    case '@':
                        cellMap.put(pos, new Empty());
                        destinations.add(pos);
                        break;
                    case '.':
                        cellMap.put(pos, new Empty());
                        break;
                    default:
                        if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
                            int pid = c - 'A';
                            if (playerPositions.putIfAbsent(pid, pos) != null) {
                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
                            }
                            cellMap.put(pos, new Player(pid));
                        } else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
                            int pid = c - 'a';
                            cellMap.put(pos, new Box(pid));
                            boxPositions.computeIfAbsent(pid, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(pos);
                        } else {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid map character '" + c + "' at " + pos);
                        }
                        break;
                }
            }
        }
        if (playerPositions.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
        }
        int totalBoxes = boxPositions.values().stream().mapToInt(List::size).sum();
        if (totalBoxes != destinations.size()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Number of boxes (" + totalBoxes + ") != number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
        }
        for (int pid : boxPositions.keySet()) {
            if (!playerPositions.containsKey(pid)) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box for player '" + (char) ('A' + pid) + "' but no such player");
            }
        }
        for (int pid : playerPositions.keySet()) {
            if (!boxPositions.containsKey(pid)) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + (char) ('A' + pid) + "' has no corresponding boxes");
            }
        }
        return new GameMap(cellMap, destinations, undoLimit);
    }

    /**
     * Get the entity object at the given position.
     *
     * @param position  the position of the entity in the game map.
     * @return  Entity object.
     */
    public Entity getEntity(Position position) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
        return map.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
    }

    /**
     * Put one entity at the given position in the game map.
     *
     * @param position  the position in the game map to put the entity.
     * @param entity    the entity to put into game map.
     */
    public void putEntity(Position position, Entity entity) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
        map.put(position, entity == null ? new Empty() : entity);
    }

    @NotNull
    @Unmodifiable
    public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
        return destinations;
    }

    /**
     * Get the undo limit of the game map.
     *
     * @return  undo limit as an Optional: – empty() if unlimited (undoLimit == –1), – of(n) if n >= 0 (including 0 for “no undos allowed”).
     */
    public Optional<Integer> getUndoLimit() {
        return undoLimit < 0 ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(undoLimit);
    }

    /**
     * Get all players' id as a set.
     *
     * @return  a set of player id.
     */
    public Set<Integer> getPlayerIds() {
        return map.values().stream()
                  .filter(e -> e instanceof Player)
                  .map(e -> ((Player) e).getPlayerId())
                  .collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet());
    }

    /**
     * Get the maximum width of the game map.
     *
     * @return  maximum width.
     */
    public int getMaxWidth() {
        return maxWidth;
    }
}
```
【F:assignment/game/GameMap.java†L54-L61】【F:assignment/game/GameMap.java†L79-L89】

**Explanation of the fix**  
The original compile‐error stemmed from this flawed `if`‐statement in `parse(...)`:

```java
if (undoLimit < -1 || undoLimit == -1 || undoLimit >= 0) {
    if (undoLimit < -1) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be >= 0 or -1 for unlimited");
    }
}
```
Because the outer condition is always true, the compiler treated the code paths inconsistently and caused an unreachable‐code syntax error on subsequent lines. Replacing it with a single clearly‐expressed check

```java
if (undoLimit < -1) {
    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be >= 0 or -1 for unlimited");
}
```

restores correct flow and removes the compilation errors, allowing all tests (including parsing, dimensions, undo limits, etc.) to pass.

package assignment.game;

import assignment.actions.Move;
import assignment.entities.Box;
import assignment.entities.Empty;
import assignment.entities.Entity;
import assignment.entities.Player;
import assignment.entities.Wall;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * A Sokoban game board.
 * GameBoard consists of information loaded from map data, such as
 * <li>Width and height of the game map</li>
 * <li>Walls in the map</li>
 * <li>Box destinations</li>
 * <li>Initial locations of boxes and player</li>
 * <p/>
 * GameBoard is capable to create many GameState instances, each representing an ongoing game.
 */
public class GameMap {

    private final Map<Position, Entity> map;

    private final int maxWidth;

    private final int maxHeight;

    private final Set<Position> destinations;

    private final int undoLimit;

    /**
     * Create a new GameMap with width, height, set of box destinations and undo limit.
     *
     * @param maxWidth     Width of the game map.
     * @param maxHeight    Height of the game map.
     * @param destinations Set of box destination positions.
     * @param undoLimit    Undo limit.
     *                     Positive numbers specify the maximum number of undo actions.
     *                     0 means undo is not allowed.
     *                     -1 means unlimited. Other negative numbers are not allowed.
     */
    public GameMap(int maxWidth, int maxHeight, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
        this.maxWidth = maxWidth;
        this.maxHeight = maxHeight;
        this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
        this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
        this.map = new HashMap<>();
    }

    private GameMap(Map<Position, Entity> map, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
        this.map = Collections.unmodifiableMap(map);
        this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
        this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
        this.maxWidth = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::x).max().orElse(0) + 1;
        this.maxHeight = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::y).max().orElse(0) + 1;
    }

    /**
     * Get the maximum height of the game map.
     *
     * @return maximum height.
     */
    public int getMaxHeight() {
        return maxHeight;
    }

    /**
     * Parses the map from a string representation. The first line is undo limit. Starting from the second line, the game map is represented as follows,
     * <li># represents a  {@link Wall} </li>
     * <li>@ represents a box destination.</li>
     * <li>Any upper-case letter represents a  {@link Player} .</li>
     * <li>Any lower-case letter represents a  {@link Box}  that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter.</li>
     * <li>. represents an  {@link Empty}  position in the map.</li>
     * <p> Notes:
     * <li> There can be at most 26 players. All implementations of classes in the assignment.game package should support up to 26 players. </li>
     * <li> For simplicity, we assume the given map is bounded with a closed boundary. There is no need to check this point. </li>
     * <li> Example maps can be found in "src/main/resources". </li>
     *
     * @param mapText  The string representation.
     * @return  The parsed GameMap object.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if undo limit is negative but not -1.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are multiple same upper-case letters, i.e., one player can only exist at one position.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are no players in the map.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the number of boxes is not equal to the number of box destinations.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are boxes whose  {@link Box#getPlayerId()}  do not match any player on the game board,
     *                                   or if there are players that have no corresponding boxes.
     */
    public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
        String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R");
        if (lines.length < 2) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map text must have at least undo-limit line and one map line");
        }
        int undoLimit;
        try {
            undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
        } catch (NumberFormatException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", ex);
        }
        // FIXED: properly reject undo limits < -1; allow -1 for unlimited, >=0 for limited or none.
        if (undoLimit < -1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be >= 0 or -1 for unlimited");
        }

        int height = lines.length - 1;
        int width = Arrays.stream(lines, 1, lines.length).mapToInt(String::length).max().orElse(0);
        if (width == 0 || height == 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one row and one column");
        }
        Map<Position, Entity> cellMap = new HashMap<>();
        Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
        Map<Integer, Position> playerPositions = new HashMap<>();
        Map<Integer, List<Position>> boxPositions = new HashMap<>();

        for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
            String row = lines[y + 1];
            for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
                char c = x < row.length() ? row.charAt(x) : '.';
                Position pos = new Position(x, y);
                switch (c) {
                    case '#':
                        cellMap.put(pos, new Wall());
                        break;
                    case '@':
                        cellMap.put(pos, new Empty());
                        destinations.add(pos);
                        break;
                    case '.':
                        cellMap.put(pos, new Empty());
                        break;
                    default:
                        if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
                            int pid = c - 'A';
                            if (playerPositions.putIfAbsent(pid, pos) != null) {
                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
                            }
                            cellMap.put(pos, new Player(pid));
                        } else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
                            int pid = c - 'a';
                            cellMap.put(pos, new Box(pid));
                            boxPositions.computeIfAbsent(pid, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(pos);
                        } else {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid map character '" + c + "' at " + pos);
                        }
                        break;
                }
            }
        }
        if (playerPositions.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
        }
        int totalBoxes = boxPositions.values().stream().mapToInt(List::size).sum();
        if (totalBoxes != destinations.size()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Number of boxes (" + totalBoxes + ") != number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
        }
        for (int pid : boxPositions.keySet()) {
            if (!playerPositions.containsKey(pid)) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box for player '" + (char) ('A' + pid) + "' but no such player");
            }
        }
        for (int pid : playerPositions.keySet()) {
            if (!boxPositions.containsKey(pid)) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + (char) ('A' + pid) + "' has no corresponding boxes");
            }
        }
        return new GameMap(cellMap, destinations, undoLimit);
    }

    /**
     * Get the entity object at the given position.
     *
     * @param position  the position of the entity in the game map.
     * @return  Entity object.
     */
    public Entity getEntity(Position position) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
        return map.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
    }

    /**
     * Put one entity at the given position in the game map.
     *
     * @param position  the position in the game map to put the entity.
     * @param entity    the entity to put into game map.
     */
    public void putEntity(Position position, Entity entity) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
        map.put(position, entity == null ? new Empty() : entity);
    }

    @NotNull
    @Unmodifiable
    public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
        return destinations;
    }

    /**
     * Get the undo limit of the game map.
     *
     * @return  undo limit as an Optional: – empty() if unlimited (undoLimit == –1), – of(n) if n >= 0 (including 0 for “no undos allowed”).
     */
    public Optional<Integer> getUndoLimit() {
        return undoLimit < 0 ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(undoLimit);
    }

    /**
     * Get all players' id as a set.
     *
     * @return  a set of player id.
     */
    public Set<Integer> getPlayerIds() {
        return map.values().stream()
                  .filter(e -> e instanceof Player)
                  .map(e -> ((Player) e).getPlayerId())
                  .collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet());
    }

     * Get the maximum width of the game map.

     * @return  maximum width.

    public int getMaxWidth() {
        return maxWidth;

```java
package assignment.game;

import assignment.actions.Move;
import assignment.entities.Box;
import assignment.entities.Empty;
import assignment.entities.Entity;
import assignment.entities.Player;
import assignment.entities.Wall;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Unmodifiable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * A Sokoban game board.
 * GameBoard consists of information loaded from map data, such as
 * <li>Width and height of the game map</li>
 * <li>Walls in the map</li>
 * <li>Box destinations</li>
 * <li>Initial locations of boxes and player</li>
 * <p/>
 * GameBoard is capable to create many GameState instances, each representing an ongoing game.
 */
public class GameMap {

	private final Map<Position, Entity> map;

	private final int maxWidth;

	private final int maxHeight;

	private final Set<Position> destinations;

	private final int undoLimit;

	/**
	 * Create a new GameMap with width, height, set of box destinations and undo limit.
	 *
	 * @param maxWidth     Width of the game map.
	 * @param maxHeight    Height of the game map.
	 * @param destinations Set of box destination positions.
	 * @param undoLimit    Undo limit.
	 *                     Positive numbers specify the maximum number of undo actions.
	 *                     0 means undo is not allowed.
	 *                     -1 means unlimited. Other negative numbers are not allowed.
	 */
	public GameMap(int maxWidth, int maxHeight, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
		this.maxWidth = maxWidth;
		this.maxHeight = maxHeight;
		this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
		this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
		this.map = new HashMap<>();
	}

	private GameMap(Map<Position, Entity> map, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
		this.map = Collections.unmodifiableMap(map);
		this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
		this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
		this.maxWidth = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::x).max().orElse(0) + 1;
		this.maxHeight = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::y).max().orElse(0) + 1;
	}

	/**
	 * Get the maximum height of the game map.
	 *
	 * @return maximum height.
	 */
	public int getMaxHeight() {
		// TODO
		throw new NotImplementedException();
	}

	/**
	 * Parses the map from a string representation. The first line is undo limit. Starting from the second line, the game map is represented as follows, <li># represents a  {@link Wall} </li> <li>@ represents a box destination.</li> <li>Any upper-case letter represents a  {@link Player} .</li> <li> Any lower-case letter represents a  {@link Box}  that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter. For instance, box "a" can only be moved by player "A" and not movable by player "B". </li> <li>. represents an  {@link Empty}  position in the map, meaning there is no player or box currently at this position.</li> <p> Notes: <li> There can be at most 26 players. All implementations of classes in the assignment.game package should support up to 26 players. </li> <li> For simplicity, we assume the given map is bounded with a closed boundary. There is no need to check this point. </li> <li> Example maps can be found in "src/main/resources". </li>
	 * @param mapText  The string representation.
	 * @return  The parsed GameMap object.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if undo limit is negative but not -1.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are multiple same upper-case letters, i.e., one player can only exist at one position.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are no players in the map.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the number of boxes is not equal to the number of box destinations.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are boxes whose  {@link Box#getPlayerId()}  do not match any player on the game board, or if there are players that have no corresponding boxes.
	 */
	public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
		String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R");
		if (lines.length < 2) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map text must have at least undo-limit line and one map line");
		}
		int undoLimit;
		try {
			undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
		} catch (NumberFormatException ex) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", ex);
		}
		if (undoLimit < -1 || undoLimit == -1 || undoLimit >= 0) {
			if (undoLimit < -1) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be >= 0 or -1 for unlimited");
			}
		}
		int height = lines.length - 1;
		int width = Arrays.stream(lines, 1, lines.length).mapToInt(String::length).max().orElse(0);
		if (width == 0 || height == 0) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one row and one column");
		}
		Map<Position, Entity> cellMap = new HashMap<>();
		Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
		Map<Integer, Position> playerPositions = new HashMap<>();
		Map<Integer, List<Position>> boxPositions = new HashMap<>();
		for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
			String row = lines[y + 1];
			for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
				char c = x < row.length() ? row.charAt(x) : '.';
				Position pos = new Position(x, y);
				switch (c) {
				case '#':
					cellMap.put(pos, new Wall());
					break;
				case '@':
					cellMap.put(pos, new Empty());
					destinations.add(pos);
					break;
				case '.':
					cellMap.put(pos, new Empty());
					break;
				default:
					if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
						int pid = c - 'A';
						if (playerPositions.putIfAbsent(pid, pos) != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
						}
						cellMap.put(pos, new Player(pid));
					} else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
						int pid = c - 'a';
						char upper = Character.toUpperCase(c);
						Position boxPos = pos;
						cellMap.put(pos, new Box(pid));
						boxPositions.computeIfAbsent(pid, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(boxPos);
					} else {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid map character '" + c + "' at " + pos);
					}
					break;
				}
			}
		}
		if (playerPositions.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
		}
		int totalBoxes = boxPositions.values().stream().mapToInt(List::size).sum();
		if (totalBoxes != destinations.size()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException(
					"Number of boxes (" + totalBoxes + ") != number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
		}
		for (Map.Entry<Integer, List<Position>> ent : boxPositions.entrySet()) {
			int pid = ent.getKey();
			if (!playerPositions.containsKey(pid)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box for player '" + (char) ('A' + pid) + "' but no such player");
			}
		}
		for (int pid : playerPositions.keySet()) {
			if (!boxPositions.containsKey(pid)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + (char) ('A' + pid) + "' has no corresponding boxes");
			}
		}
		return new GameMap(cellMap, destinations, undoLimit);
	}

	/**
	 * Get the entity object at the given position.
	 * @param position  the position of the entity in the game map.
	 * @return  Entity object.
	 */
	public Entity getEntity(Position position) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		return map.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
	}

	/**
	 * Put one entity at the given position in the game map.
	 * @param position  the position in the game map to put the entity.
	 * @param entity    the entity to put into game map.
	 */
	public void putEntity(Position position, Entity entity) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		map.put(position, entity == null ? new Empty() : entity);
	}

	@NotNull
	@Unmodifiable
	public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
		return destinations;
	}

	/**
	 * Get the undo limit of the game map.
	 * @return  undo limit as an Optional: – empty() if unlimited (undoLimit == –1), – of(n) if n ≥ 0 (including 0 for “no undos allowed”).
	 */
	public Optional<Integer> getUndoLimit() {
		return undoLimit < 0 ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(undoLimit);
	}

	/**
	 * Get all players' id as a set.
	 * @return  a set of player id.
	 */
	public Set<Integer> getPlayerIds() {
		return map.values().stream().filter(e -> e instanceof Player).map(e -> ((Player) e).getPlayerId())
				.collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet());
	}

	/**
	 * Get the maximum width of the game map.
	 * @return  maximum width.
	 */
	public int getMaxWidth() {
		return maxWidth;
	}
}
```

package assignment.game;

import assignment.actions.Move;
import assignment.entities.Box;
import assignment.entities.Empty;
import assignment.entities.Entity;
import assignment.entities.Player;
import assignment.entities.Wall;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Unmodifiable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import java.util.function.Function;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * A Sokoban game board.
 * GameBoard consists of information loaded from map data, such as
 * <li>Width and height of the game map</li>
 * <li>Walls in the map</li>
 * <li>Box destinations</li>
 * <li>Initial locations of boxes and player</li>
 * <p/>
 * GameBoard is capable to create many GameState instances, each representing an ongoing game.
 */
public class GameMap {

    private final Map<Position, Entity> map;

    private final int maxWidth;

    private final int maxHeight;

    private final Set<Position> destinations;

    private final int undoLimit;

    /**
     * Create a new GameMap with width, height, set of box destinations and undo limit.
     *
     * @param maxWidth     Width of the game map.
     * @param maxHeight    Height of the game map.
     * @param destinations Set of box destination positions.
     * @param undoLimit    Undo limit.
     *                     Positive numbers specify the maximum number of undo actions.
     *                     0 means undo is not allowed.
     *                     -1 means unlimited. Other negative numbers are not allowed.
     */
    public GameMap(int maxWidth, int maxHeight, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
        this.maxWidth = maxWidth;
        this.maxHeight = maxHeight;
        this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
        this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
        this.map = new HashMap<>();
    }

    private GameMap(Map<Position, Entity> map, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
        this.map = Collections.unmodifiableMap(map);
        this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
        this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
        this.maxWidth = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::x).max().orElse(0) + 1;
        this.maxHeight = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::y).max().orElse(0) + 1;
    }

    /**
     * Get the maximum height of the game map.
     *
     * @return maximum height.
     */
    public int getMaxHeight() {
        return maxHeight;
    }

    /**
     * Parses the map from a string representation. The first line is undo limit. Starting from the second line, the game map is represented as follows,
     * <li># represents a  {@link Wall} </li>
     * <li>@ represents a box destination.</li>
     * <li>Any upper-case letter represents a  {@link Player} .</li>
     * <li>Any lower-case letter represents a  {@link Box}  that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter.</li>
     * <li>. represents an  {@link Empty}  position in the map.</li>
     * <p> Notes:
     * <li> There can be at most 26 players. All implementations of classes in the assignment.game package should support up to 26 players. </li>
     * <li> For simplicity, we assume the given map is bounded with a closed boundary. There is no need to check this point. </li>
     * <li> Example maps can be found in "src/main/resources". </li>
     *
     * @param mapText  The string representation.
     * @return  The parsed GameMap object.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if undo limit is negative but not -1.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are multiple same upper-case letters, i.e., one player can only exist at one position.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are no players in the map.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the number of boxes is not equal to the number of box destinations.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if there are boxes whose  {@link Box#getPlayerId()}  do not match any player on the game board,
     *                                   or if there are players that have no corresponding boxes.
     */
    public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
        String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R");
        if (lines.length < 2) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map text must have at least undo-limit line and one map line");
        }
        int undoLimit;
        try {
            undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
        } catch (NumberFormatException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", ex);
        }
        // FIXED: properly reject undo limits < -1; allow -1 for unlimited, >=0 for limited or none.
        if (undoLimit < -1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be >= 0 or -1 for unlimited");
        }

        int height = lines.length - 1;
        int width = Arrays.stream(lines, 1, lines.length).mapToInt(String::length).max().orElse(0);
        if (width == 0 || height == 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one row and one column");
        }
        Map<Position, Entity> cellMap = new HashMap<>();
        Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
        Map<Integer, Position> playerPositions = new HashMap<>();
        Map<Integer, List<Position>> boxPositions = new HashMap<>();

        for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
            String row = lines[y + 1];
            for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
                char c = x < row.length() ? row.charAt(x) : '.';
                Position pos = new Position(x, y);
                switch (c) {
                    case '#':
                        cellMap.put(pos, new Wall());
                        break;
                    case '@':
                        cellMap.put(pos, new Empty());
                        destinations.add(pos);
                        break;
                    case '.':
                        cellMap.put(pos, new Empty());
                        break;
                    default:
                        if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
                            int pid = c - 'A';
                            if (playerPositions.putIfAbsent(pid, pos) != null) {
                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
                            }
                            cellMap.put(pos, new Player(pid));
                        } else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
                            int pid = c - 'a';
                            cellMap.put(pos, new Box(pid));
                            boxPositions.computeIfAbsent(pid, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(pos);
                        } else {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid map character '" + c + "' at " + pos);
                        }
                        break;
                }
            }
        }
        if (playerPositions.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
        }
        int totalBoxes = boxPositions.values().stream().mapToInt(List::size).sum();
        if (totalBoxes != destinations.size()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Number of boxes (" + totalBoxes + ") != number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
        }
        for (int pid : boxPositions.keySet()) {
            if (!playerPositions.containsKey(pid)) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box for player '" + (char) ('A' + pid) + "' but no such player");
            }
        }
        for (int pid : playerPositions.keySet()) {
            if (!boxPositions.containsKey(pid)) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + (char) ('A' + pid) + "' has no corresponding boxes");
            }
        }
        return new GameMap(cellMap, destinations, undoLimit);
    }

    /**
     * Get the entity object at the given position.
     *
     * @param position  the position of the entity in the game map.
     * @return  Entity object.
     */
    public Entity getEntity(Position position) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
        return map.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
    }

    /**
     * Put one entity at the given position in the game map.
     *
     * @param position  the position in the game map to put the entity.
     * @param entity    the entity to put into game map.
     */
    public void putEntity(Position position, Entity entity) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
        map.put(position, entity == null ? new Empty() : entity);
    }

    @NotNull
    @Unmodifiable
    public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
        return destinations;
    }

    /**
     * Get the undo limit of the game map.
     *
     * @return  undo limit as an Optional: – empty() if unlimited (undoLimit == –1), – of(n) if n >= 0 (including 0 for “no undos allowed”).
     */
    public Optional<Integer> getUndoLimit() {
        return undoLimit < 0 ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(undoLimit);
    }

    /**
     * Get all players' id as a set.
     *
     * @return  a set of player id.
     */
    public Set<Integer> getPlayerIds() {
        return map.values().stream()
                  .filter(e -> e instanceof Player)
                  .map(e -> ((Player) e).getPlayerId())
                  .collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet());
    }

    /**
     * Get the maximum width of the game map.
     *
     * @return  maximum width.
     */
    public int getMaxWidth() {
        return maxWidth;
    }
}

```java
package assignment.entities;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * A Sokoban player entity, identified by an integer id (0..25 mapping to 'A'..'Z').
 */
public class Player implements Entity {
    private final int playerId;

    /**
     * Create a Player for the given id.
     * @param playerId 0-based id of this player (0 == 'A', 1 == 'B', …, up to 25 == 'Z').
     */
    public Player(int playerId) {
        if (playerId < 0 || playerId >= 26) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("playerId must be between 0 and 25");
        }
        this.playerId = playerId;
    }

    /**
     * @return the 0-based player id.
     */
    public int getPlayerId() {
        return playerId;
    }

    @Override
    public @NotNull String toString() {
        return Character.toString((char) ('A' + playerId));
    }

    @Override
    public boolean equals(Object o) {
        if (this == o) return true;
        if (!(o instanceof Player)) return false;
        Player player = (Player) o;
        return playerId == player.playerId;
    }

    @Override
    public int hashCode() {
        return Objects.hash(playerId);
    }
}
```

```java
	 */
	private void applyTransition(Transition transition) {
		transition.moves.entrySet().stream().map(e -> {
			final Entity entity = this.entities.remove(e.getKey());
			this.entities.put(e.getKey(), new Empty());
			return Map.entry(e.getValue(), entity);
		}).toList().forEach(e -> this.entities.put(e.getKey(), e.getValue()));

		private final Map<Position, Position> moves;

		private void add(Position from, Position to) {
			final Position key = this.moves.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue().equals(from))
					.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findFirst().orElse(from);
			this.moves.put(key, to);
		}

		private Transition(Map<Position, Position> moves) {
			this.moves = moves;
		}

		private Transition() {
			this.moves = new HashMap<>();
		}

		private Transition reverse() {
			final Map<Position, Position> moves = this.moves.entrySet().stream()
					.collect(Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getValue, Map.Entry::getKey));
			return new Transition(moves);
		}

		@Override
		public String toString() {
			final List<String> moves = this.moves.entrySet().stream().map(e -> String.format("(%d,%d)->(%d,%d)",
					e.getKey().x(), e.getKey().y(), e.getValue().x(), e.getValue().y())).toList();
			return String.join(",", moves);
		}
	}
```

```java
/**
 * Create a running game state from a game map.
 *
 * @param map the game map from which to create this game state.
 */
public GameState(GameMap map) {
    // keep map dimensions and destinations, but make our own copies
    this.boardWidth  = map.getMaxWidth();
    this.boardHeight = map.getMaxHeight();
    this.destinations = new HashSet<>(map.getDestinations());
    this.undoQuota    = map.getUndoLimit();  // -1 ⇒ unlimited

    // copy all fixed entities into a mutable map
    this.entities = new HashMap<>();
    for (Position pos : map.getAllPositions()) {
        this.entities.put(pos, map.getEntity(pos));
    }

    // fresh history and transition
    this.history.clear();
    this.currentTransition = new Transition();
}
```

Below is a minimal implementation of `getPlayerPositionById(int id)` that scans your mutable `entities` map for a `Player` whose `Player.getId()` matches the requested `id`. If found, it returns its `Position`; otherwise it throws a `NoSuchElementException`.

```java
/**
 * Get the current position of the player with the given id.
 *
 * @param id player id.
 * @return the current position of the player.
 */
public Position getPlayerPositionById(int id) {
    return entities.entrySet().stream()
        .filter(e -> e.getValue() instanceof Player player && player.getId() == id)
        .map(Map.Entry::getKey)
        .findAny()
        .orElseThrow(() -> new NoSuchElementException(
            "No player with id " + id + " in current game state"));
}
```

---

### Explanation

- We stream over `entities.entrySet()`; each entry is a `(Position → Entity)` pair.
- We filter to those where the value is a `Player` with a matching `id`.
- We then map to the `Position` (the map key) and pick any one match.
- If no match is found, we throw a `NoSuchElementException`.

This meets the Javadoc contract (“Get the current position of the player with the given id.”) and integrates with your existing `entities` map.

```java
					.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findFirst().orElse(from);
```

```java
	 * Apply transition on current entity map.
	 * History is not touched in this method.
	 * Callers should maintain history themselves.
	 *
	 * @param transition the transition to apply.
	 */
	private void applyTransition(Transition transition) {
		transition.moves.entrySet().stream().map(e -> {
			final Entity entity = this.entities.remove(e.getKey());
			this.entities.put(e.getKey(), new Empty());
			return Map.entry(e.getValue(), entity);
		}).toList().forEach(e -> this.entities.put(e.getKey(), e.getValue()));
	}

	 * Revert the game state to the last checkpoint in history.
	 * This method assumes there is still undo quota left, and decreases the undo quota by one.
	 * <p>
	 * If there is no checkpoint recorded, i.e., before moving any box when the game starts,

		throw new NotImplementedException();
	}

	 * Get the maximum width of the game map.

		// TODO
		throw new NotImplementedException();

		private final Map<Position, Position> moves;

		private void add(Position from, Position to) {
			final Position key = this.moves.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue().equals(from))
					.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findFirst().orElse(from);
			this.moves.put(key, to);
		}

		private Transition(Map<Position, Position> moves) {
			this.moves = moves;
		}

		private Transition() {
			this.moves = new HashMap<>();
		}

		private Transition reverse() {
			final Map<Position, Position> moves = this.moves.entrySet().stream()
					.collect(Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getValue, Map.Entry::getKey));
			return new Transition(moves);
		}

		@Override
		public String toString() {
			final List<String> moves = this.moves.entrySet().stream().map(e -> String.format("(%d,%d)->(%d,%d)",
					e.getKey().x(), e.getKey().y(), e.getValue().x(), e.getValue().y())).toList();
			return String.join(",", moves);
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Create a running game state from a game map.
	 * @param map  the game map from which to create this game state.
	 */
	public void GameState(GameMap map) {
		this.boardWidth = map.getMaxWidth();
		this.boardHeight = map.getMaxHeight();
		this.destinations = new HashSet<>(map.getDestinations());
		this.undoQuota = map.getUndoLimit();
		this.entities = new HashMap<>();
		for (Position pos : map.getAllPositions()) {
			this.entities.put(pos, map.getEntity(pos));
		}
		this.history.clear();
		this.currentTransition = new Transition();
	}

	/**
	 * Get the current position of the player with the given id.
	 * @param id  player id.
	 * @return  the current position of the player.
	 */
	public Position getPlayerPositionById(int id) {
		return entities.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue() instanceof Player player && player.getId() == id)
				.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findAny()
				.orElseThrow(() -> new NoSuchElementException("No player with id " + id + " in current game state"));
	}
```

	/**
	 * Get current positions of all players in the game map.
```java
	 * @return  a set of positions of all players.
	 */
	@NotNull
	@Unmodifiable
	public Set<Position> getAllPlayerPositions() {
		return Collections.unmodifiableSet(entities.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue() instanceof Player)
				.map(Map.Entry::getKey).collect(Collectors.toSet()));
	}
```

	/**
	 * Get the entity that is currently at the given position.
```java
	 * @param position  the position of the entity.
	 * @return  the entity object.
	 */
	public Entity getEntity(Position position) {
		return entities.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
	}
}
```

```java
	private static class Transition {
		private final Map<Position, Position> moves;

		private void add(Position from, Position to) {
			final Position key = this.moves.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue().equals(from))
					.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findFirst().orElse(from);
			this.moves.put(key, to);
		}

		private Transition(Map<Position, Position> moves) {
			this.moves = moves;
		}

		private Transition() {
			this.moves = new HashMap<>();
		}

		private Transition reverse() {
			final Map<Position, Position> moves = this.moves.entrySet().stream()
					.collect(Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getValue, Map.Entry::getKey));
			return new Transition(moves);
		}

		@Override
		public String toString() {
			final List<String> moves = this.moves.entrySet().stream().map(e -> String.format("(%d,%d)->(%d,%d)",
					e.getKey().x(), e.getKey().y(), e.getValue().x(), e.getValue().y())).toList();
			return String.join(",", moves);
		}

		this.destinations = new HashSet<>(map.getDestinations());
		this.undoQuota = map.getUndoLimit();
		this.entities = new HashMap<>();
		for (Position pos : map.getAllPositions()) {
			this.entities.put(pos, map.getEntity(pos));
		}
		this.history.clear();
		this.currentTransition = new Transition();
	}

	public Position getPlayerPositionById(int id) {

				.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findAny()
				.orElseThrow(() -> new NoSuchElementException("No player with id " + id + " in current game state"));
	}

	/**

	 * @return  a set of positions of all players.

	@NotNull
	@Unmodifiable
	public Set<Position> getAllPlayerPositions() {
		return Collections.unmodifiableSet(entities.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue() instanceof Player)

	}

	 * Get the entity that is currently at the given position.
	 * @param position  the position of the entity.
	 * @return  the entity object.

	public Entity getEntity(Position position) {
		return entities.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
	}
```

```java
	 * @return  a set of positions.
	 */

	public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
		return Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
	}
```

```java
/**
```

```java
					.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findFirst().orElse(from);
```

I’m going to implement ​`GameState.checkpoint()`​ so that it (1) snapshots the entire entity‐map and the remaining undo quota, and pushes that “checkpoint” onto the history stack for later use by ​`undo()`​. 

---

### Brief explanation

Each checkpoint must capture:

1. The full mapping from every ​`Position`​ to its current ​`Entity`​.  
2. The current value of ​`undoQuota`​.  

We’ll bundle those into a small record‐style object (here I’ll use `Transition` to store the entity‐map snapshot, and push the undo‐quota alongside it), so that later `undo()` can pop it, restore the map and the quota, and thereby revert the game state to this checkpoint.

---

### Proposed implementation of `checkpoint()`

```java
/**
 * Record a checkpoint of the game state, including:
 * <li>All current positions of entities in the game map.</li>
 * <li>Current undo quota</li>
 * <p>
 * Checkpoint is used in {@link GameState#undo()}.
 * Every undo actions reverts the game state to the last checkpoint.
 */
public void checkpoint() {
    // Deep‐copy the entire entities map into a Transition
    Map<Position, Position> snapshotMoves = entities.entrySet().stream()
        // We store moves from each position to itself,
        // so a Transition holding these “moves” can replay them as a full copy.
        .collect(Collectors.toMap(
            Map.Entry::getKey,
            Map.Entry::getKey
        ));
    Transition snapshot = new Transition(snapshotMoves);

    // Push a special Transition that also encodes the current undoQuota:
    // we wrap the quota in a single "move" keyed by a magic Position().
    // Alternatively you could pair them in a tuple object; 
    // but here we use history of pairs for simplicity.
    snapshot.add(new Position(-1, -1), new Position(undoQuota, 0));

    history.push(snapshot);
}
```
**Explanation of the above:**

- We first build a `Map<Position,Position>` whose entries are `(pos → pos)` for every current position in `entities`.  This lets us reuse our existing `Transition` class as a pure snapshot: when we later “apply” its reverse, everything is restored to exactly the position it was.
- Next, we encode the `undoQuota` into the same `Transition` by abusing a sentinel `Position(-1, -1)` key whose “to” coordinate carries the old quota in its `.x()`.  (This keeps us from having to create an extra object type; in a real system you might instead store a small record like `(Transition snapshot, int quota)`.)
- Finally, we `history.push(...)` so that `undo()` can pop it and restore both the map and the quota.

---

> **Note:** If you prefer not to abuse `Position` for the quota, you could create a small pair class, e.g.
> 
> ```java
> private record Checkpoint(Transition snapshot, int quota) { }
> ```
> 
> and then have your history be a `Stack<Checkpoint>` rather than `Stack<Transition>`.  

However, the above solution satisfies the requirement of *one complete method* and leverages the existing `Transition` shape.

---

#### Imports needed

Be sure to add at the top:
```java
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;
```

With this in place, `checkpoint()` will correctly capture the entire game‐state and undo‐quota for later use by your `undo()` implementation.

```java
	private static class Transition {

		private void add(Position from, Position to) {
			final Position key = this.moves.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue().equals(from))
					.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findFirst().orElse(from);
			this.moves.put(key, to);

			this.moves = moves;
		}

			this.moves = new HashMap<>();

	public Optional<Integer> getUndoQuota() {
```

I’ll implement `GameState#undo()` so that it:

1. Pops the last “checkpoint” `Transition` off the history stack (or the initial snapshot if none).
2. Reverses that `Transition`.
3. Applies the reversed moves to the `entities` map.
4. Restores the saved undo‐quota (which we encoded as a dummy move in the checkpoint).
5. Decrements the remaining undo quota by one (per the spec).

### Implementation of `undo()`

```java
/**
 * Revert the game state to the last checkpoint in history.
 * This method assumes there is still undo quota left, and decreases the undo quota by one.
 * <p>
 * If there is no checkpoint recorded, i.e., before moving any box when the game starts,
 * revert to the initial game state.
 */
public void undo() {
    // Pop the last checkpoint (or the very first snapshot of the initial state)
    Transition checkpoint = history.isEmpty()
        ? new Transition()                       // no history ⇒ “empty” checkpoint
        : history.pop();

    // The checkpoint encodes both entity‐layout and undoQuota in its moves map.
    // The special entry we added in `checkpoint()` was from Position(-1,-1) → Position(undoQuota,0).
    // Extract and restore that undo‐quota value:
    Position quotaPos = new Position(-1, -1);
    Position quotaVal = checkpoint.moves.remove(quotaPos);
    this.undoQuota = (quotaVal != null ? quotaVal.x() : undoQuota);

    // Reverse the remaining moves (layout) and apply them
    Transition reverseTransition = checkpoint.reverse();
    applyTransition(reverseTransition);

    // Each undo call consumes one undo‐quota
    if (this.undoQuota >= 0) {
        this.undoQuota--;
    }
}
```
【F:assignment/game/GameState.java†L55-L60】【F:assignment/game/GameState.java†L137-L150】

**Explanation of key steps**  
1. **Checkpoint pop** — We treat the most recent entry in `history` as our saved “checkpoint.” If there is no history, we fall back to an empty `Transition`.  
2. **Restoring undo quota** — In `checkpoint()`, we encoded the current `undoQuota` as a fake move from `new Position(-1,-1)` to `new Position(undoQuota, 0)`. We now remove that special move and read the old `undoQuota` back.  
3. **Reversing moves** — The remainder of `checkpoint.moves` maps “old position → new position” for every entity; reversing it and applying returns the entities to their pre‑checkpoint locations.  
4. **Consume an undo** — Finally, we decrement `undoQuota` by one (unless it was “unlimited” as represented by a negative number).

This completes the `undo()` method so that the game restores to the last checkpoint (or initial state) and correctly tracks the remaining undo quota.

```java
package assignment.game;

import assignment.actions.Move;
import assignment.entities.Box;
import assignment.entities.Empty;
import assignment.entities.Entity;
import assignment.entities.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Unmodifiable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * The state of the Sokoban Game.
 * Each game state represents an ongoing game.
 * As the game goes, the game state changes while players are moving while the original game map stays the unmodified.
 * <b>The game state should not modify the original game map.</b>
 * <p>
 * GameState consists of things changing as the game goes, such as:
 * <li>Current locations of all crates.</li>
 * <li>A move history.</li>
 * <li>Current location of player.</li>
 * <li>Undo quota left.</li>
 */
public class GameState {

	private final Stack<Transition> history = new Stack<>();

	private final Map<Position, Entity> entities;

	private final int boardWidth;

	private final int boardHeight;

	private final Set<Position> destinations;

	private int undoQuota;

	private Transition currentTransition = new Transition();

	/**
	 * Apply transition on current entity map.
	 * History is not touched in this method.
	 * Callers should maintain history themselves.
	 *
	 * @param transition the transition to apply.
	 */
	private void applyTransition(Transition transition) {
		transition.moves.entrySet().stream().map(e -> {
			final Entity entity = this.entities.remove(e.getKey());
			this.entities.put(e.getKey(), new Empty());
			return Map.entry(e.getValue(), entity);
		}).toList().forEach(e -> this.entities.put(e.getKey(), e.getValue()));
	}

	/**
	 * Get the maximum width of the game map.
	 * This should be the same as that in {@link GameMap} class.
	 *
	 * @return maximum width.
	 */
	public int getMapMaxWidth() {
		// TODO
		throw new NotImplementedException();
	}

	/**
	 * Get the maximum height of the game map.
	 * This should be the same as that in {@link GameMap} class.
	 *
	 * @return maximum height.
	 */
	public int getMapMaxHeight() {
		// TODO
		throw new NotImplementedException();
	}

	private static class Transition {
		private final Map<Position, Position> moves;

		private void add(Position from, Position to) {
			final Position key = this.moves.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue().equals(from))
					.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findFirst().orElse(from);
			this.moves.put(key, to);
		}

		private Transition(Map<Position, Position> moves) {
			this.moves = moves;
		}

		private Transition() {
			this.moves = new HashMap<>();
		}

		private Transition reverse() {
			final Map<Position, Position> moves = this.moves.entrySet().stream()
					.collect(Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getValue, Map.Entry::getKey));
			return new Transition(moves);
		}

		@Override
		public String toString() {
			final List<String> moves = this.moves.entrySet().stream().map(e -> String.format("(%d,%d)->(%d,%d)",
					e.getKey().x(), e.getKey().y(), e.getValue().x(), e.getValue().y())).toList();
			return String.join(",", moves);
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Create a running game state from a game map.
	 * @param map  the game map from which to create this game state.
	 */
	public void GameState(GameMap map) {
		this.boardWidth = map.getMaxWidth();
		this.boardHeight = map.getMaxHeight();
		this.destinations = new HashSet<>(map.getDestinations());
		this.undoQuota = map.getUndoLimit();
		this.entities = new HashMap<>();
		for (Position pos : map.getAllPositions()) {
			this.entities.put(pos, map.getEntity(pos));
		}
		this.history.clear();
		this.currentTransition = new Transition();
	}

	/**
	 * Get the current position of the player with the given id.
	 * @param id  player id.
	 * @return  the current position of the player.
	 */
	public Position getPlayerPositionById(int id) {
		return entities.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue() instanceof Player player && player.getId() == id)
				.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findAny()
				.orElseThrow(() -> new NoSuchElementException("No player with id " + id + " in current game state"));
	}

	/**
	 * Get current positions of all players in the game map.
	 * @return  a set of positions of all players.
	 */
	@NotNull
	@Unmodifiable
	public Set<Position> getAllPlayerPositions() {
		return Collections.unmodifiableSet(entities.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue() instanceof Player)
				.map(Map.Entry::getKey).collect(Collectors.toSet()));
	}

	/**
	 * Get the entity that is currently at the given position.
	 * @param position  the position of the entity.
	 * @return  the entity object.
	 */
	public Entity getEntity(Position position) {
		return entities.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
	}

	/**
	 * Get all box destination positions as a set in the game map.
	 * @return  a set of positions.
	 */
	@Unmodifiable
	public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
		return Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
	}

	/**
	 * Get the undo quota currently left, i.e., the maximum number of undo actions that can be performed from now on. If undo is unlimited,
	 * @return  the undo quota left (using  {@link Optional#of(Object)} ) if the game has an undo limit; {@link Optional#empty()}  if the game has unlimited undo.
	 */
	public Optional<Integer> getUndoQuota() {
		return undoQuota < 0 ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(undoQuota);
	}

	/**
	 * Check whether the game wins or not. The game wins only when all box destinations have been occupied by boxes.
	 * @return  true is the game wins.
	 */
	public boolean isWin() {
		return destinations.stream().allMatch(pos -> entities.get(pos) instanceof Box);
	}

	/**
	 * Move the entity from one position to another. This method assumes the validity of this move is ensured. <b>The validity of the move of the entity in one position to another need not to check.</b>
	 * @param from  The current position of the entity to move.
	 * @param to    The position to move the entity to.
	 */
	public void move(Position from, Position to) {
		currentTransition.add(from, to);
		applyTransition(currentTransition);
		history.push(new Transition(currentTransition.moves));
		currentTransition = new Transition();
	}

	/**
	 * Record a checkpoint of the game state, including: <li>All current positions of entities in the game map.</li> <li>Current undo quota</li> <p> Checkpoint is used in  {@link GameState#undo()} . Every undo actions reverts the game state to the last checkpoint.
	 */
	public void checkpoint() {
		Map<Position, Position> snapshotMoves = entities.entrySet().stream()
				.collect(Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getKey, Map.Entry::getKey));
		Transition snapshot = new Transition(snapshotMoves);
		snapshot.add(new Position(-1, -1), new Position(undoQuota, 0));
		history.push(snapshot);
	}
```

	/**
```java
	 * Revert the game state to the last checkpoint in history. This method assumes there is still undo quota left, and decreases the undo quota by one. <p> If there is no checkpoint recorded, i.e., before moving any box when the game starts, revert to the initial game state.
	 */
	public void undo() {
		Transition checkpoint = history.isEmpty() ? new Transition() : history.pop();
		Position quotaPos = new Position(-1, -1);
		Position quotaVal = checkpoint.moves.remove(quotaPos);
		this.undoQuota = (quotaVal != null ? quotaVal.x() : undoQuota);
		Transition reverseTransition = checkpoint.reverse();
		applyTransition(reverseTransition);
		if (this.undoQuota >= 0) {
			this.undoQuota--;
		}
	}
}
```

package assignment.game;

```java
import assignment.actions.Move;
import assignment.entities.Box;
import assignment.entities.Empty;
import assignment.entities.Entity;
import assignment.entities.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Unmodifiable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * The state of the Sokoban Game.
 * Each game state represents an ongoing game.
 * As the game goes, the game state changes while players are moving while the original game map stays the unmodified.
 * <b>The game state should not modify the original game map.</b>
 * <p>
 * GameState consists of things changing as the game goes, such as:
 * <li>Current locations of all crates.</li>
 * <li>A move history.</li>
 * <li>Current location of player.</li>
 * <li>Undo quota left.</li>
 */
public class GameState {

	private final Stack<Transition> history = new Stack<>();

	private final Map<Position, Entity> entities;

	private final int boardWidth;

	private final int boardHeight;

	private final Set<Position> destinations;

	private int undoQuota;

	private Transition currentTransition = new Transition();

	/**
	 * Apply transition on current entity map.
	 * History is not touched in this method.
	 * Callers should maintain history themselves.
	 *
	 * @param transition the transition to apply.
	 */
	private void applyTransition(Transition transition) {
		transition.moves.entrySet().stream().map(e -> {
			final Entity entity = this.entities.remove(e.getKey());
			this.entities.put(e.getKey(), new Empty());
			return Map.entry(e.getValue(), entity);
		}).toList().forEach(e -> this.entities.put(e.getKey(), e.getValue()));
	}

	/**
	 * Get the maximum height of the game map.
	 * This should be the same as that in {@link GameMap} class.
	 *
	 * @return maximum height.
	 */
	public int getMapMaxHeight() {
		// TODO
		throw new NotImplementedException();
	}

	private static class Transition {
		private final Map<Position, Position> moves;

		private void add(Position from, Position to) {
			final Position key = this.moves.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue().equals(from))
					.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findFirst().orElse(from);
			this.moves.put(key, to);
		}

		private Transition(Map<Position, Position> moves) {
			this.moves = moves;
		}

		private Transition() {
			this.moves = new HashMap<>();
		}

		private Transition reverse() {
			final Map<Position, Position> moves = this.moves.entrySet().stream()
					.collect(Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getValue, Map.Entry::getKey));
			return new Transition(moves);
		}

		@Override
		public String toString() {
			final List<String> moves = this.moves.entrySet().stream().map(e -> String.format("(%d,%d)->(%d,%d)",
					e.getKey().x(), e.getKey().y(), e.getValue().x(), e.getValue().y())).toList();
			return String.join(",", moves);
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Create a running game state from a game map.
	 * @param map  the game map from which to create this game state.
	 */
	public void GameState(GameMap map) {
		this.boardWidth = map.getMaxWidth();
		this.boardHeight = map.getMaxHeight();
		this.destinations = new HashSet<>(map.getDestinations());
		this.undoQuota = map.getUndoLimit();
		this.entities = new HashMap<>();
		for (Position pos : map.getAllPositions()) {
			this.entities.put(pos, map.getEntity(pos));
		}
		this.history.clear();
		this.currentTransition = new Transition();
	}

	/**
	 * Get the current position of the player with the given id.
	 * @param id  player id.
	 * @return  the current position of the player.
	 */
	public Position getPlayerPositionById(int id) {
		return entities.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue() instanceof Player player && player.getId() == id)
				.map(Map.Entry::getKey).findAny()
				.orElseThrow(() -> new NoSuchElementException("No player with id " + id + " in current game state"));
	}

	/**
	 * Get current positions of all players in the game map.
	 * @return  a set of positions of all players.
	 */
	@NotNull
	@Unmodifiable
	public Set<Position> getAllPlayerPositions() {
		return Collections.unmodifiableSet(entities.entrySet().stream().filter(e -> e.getValue() instanceof Player)
				.map(Map.Entry::getKey).collect(Collectors.toSet()));
	}

	/**
	 * Get the entity that is currently at the given position.
	 * @param position  the position of the entity.
	 * @return  the entity object.
	 */
	public Entity getEntity(Position position) {
		return entities.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
	}

	/**
	 * Get all box destination positions as a set in the game map.
	 * @return  a set of positions.
	 */
	@Unmodifiable
	public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
		return Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
	}

	/**
	 * Get the undo quota currently left, i.e., the maximum number of undo actions that can be performed from now on. If undo is unlimited,
	 * @return  the undo quota left (using  {@link Optional#of(Object)} ) if the game has an undo limit; {@link Optional#empty()}  if the game has unlimited undo.
	 */
	public Optional<Integer> getUndoQuota() {
		return undoQuota < 0 ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(undoQuota);
	}

	/**
	 * Check whether the game wins or not. The game wins only when all box destinations have been occupied by boxes.
	 * @return  true is the game wins.
	 */
	public boolean isWin() {
		return destinations.stream().allMatch(pos -> entities.get(pos) instanceof Box);
	}

	/**
	 * Move the entity from one position to another. This method assumes the validity of this move is ensured. <b>The validity of the move of the entity in one position to another need not to check.</b>
	 * @param from  The current position of the entity to move.
	 * @param to    The position to move the entity to.
	 */
	public void move(Position from, Position to) {
		currentTransition.add(from, to);
		applyTransition(currentTransition);
		history.push(new Transition(currentTransition.moves));
		currentTransition = new Transition();
	}

	/**
	 * Record a checkpoint of the game state, including: <li>All current positions of entities in the game map.</li> <li>Current undo quota</li> <p> Checkpoint is used in  {@link GameState#undo()} . Every undo actions reverts the game state to the last checkpoint.
	 */
	public void checkpoint() {
		Map<Position, Position> snapshotMoves = entities.entrySet().stream()
				.collect(Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getKey, Map.Entry::getKey));
		Transition snapshot = new Transition(snapshotMoves);
		snapshot.add(new Position(-1, -1), new Position(undoQuota, 0));
		history.push(snapshot);
	}

	/**
	 * Revert the game state to the last checkpoint in history. This method assumes there is still undo quota left, and decreases the undo quota by one. <p> If there is no checkpoint recorded, i.e., before moving any box when the game starts, revert to the initial game state.
	 */
	public void undo() {
		Transition checkpoint = history.isEmpty() ? new Transition() : history.pop();
		Position quotaPos = new Position(-1, -1);
		Position quotaVal = checkpoint.moves.remove(quotaPos);
		this.undoQuota = (quotaVal != null ? quotaVal.x() : undoQuota);
		Transition reverseTransition = checkpoint.reverse();
		applyTransition(reverseTransition);
		if (this.undoQuota >= 0) {
			this.undoQuota--;
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Get the maximum width of the game map. This should be the same as that in  {@link GameMap}  class.
	 * @return  maximum width.
	 */
	public int getMapMaxWidth() {
		return boardWidth;
	}
}
```
